lesson.title: Emotion inference at work and in education
lesson.summary: Check biometric emotion inference in workplace/education settings and the exact medical/safety boundary.

prerequisites.reason: The prohibition concerns emotion inference from the biometric basis already defined.
The setting and intended purpose must be checked as elements of the ban.

blocks: The **emotion-setting ban** concerns AI used to infer a person's emotions in workplaces or education institutions, with a stated exception for systems intended for medical or safety reasons.

First establish biometric emotion/intent inference under the definition, the setting and the regulated action. A sentiment questionnaire and facial emotion inference are not interchangeable just because both concern feelings.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 3(39), Article 5(1)(f), recital 18; Annex III 1(c)

blocks: The **medical/safety boundary** requires examining the actual intended use. Calling performance monitoring 'wellbeing' or 'safety' does not establish the exception.

Fictional Northbridge employer infers emotions from facial signals to score motivation. A generic wellbeing claim is insufficient evidence of a medical or safety purpose. Assess precise facts rather than promises.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 3(39), Article 5(1)(f), recital 18; Annex III 1(c)

blocks: Recital 18 distinguishes physical states such as pain or fatigue from emotions or intentions. A driver-fatigue detector for accident prevention is not automatically emotion recognition.
Do not reason that every bodily-state detector requires an emotion exception. Establish what the system infers. Other safety, product, personal-data or high-risk rules can remain relevant.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 3(39), Article 5(1)(f), recital 18; Annex III 1(c)

blocks: If a permitted medical/safety emotion use is established, that is a narrow prohibition result. Annex III emotion classification, transparency and other law still require checks.
Record the inferred state, biometric basis, workplace/education context and purpose evidence. A consent form is not supplied here as a blanket cure for prohibited workplace inference.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 3(39), Article 5(1)(f), recital 18; Annex III 1(c)
